newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says can weather any attacks on peso.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says can weather any attacks on peso.

text.p: The Philippines can still cope with any challenges against the peso and is on track for continued high growth and low inflation, despite the recent plunge in the currency, President Fidel Ramos said.
"We have weathered the challenge and we will continue to do so," he told a dinner on Friday night.
The economy was sound and the government committed to sustaining growth, he said.
The Philippines was forced earlier this month to allow a devaluation in the peso after repeated speculative attacks began to eat up too much of its foreign exchange reserves.
"The economy will remain on track and on the upside of growth," Ramos said.
"We can hold the line against inflation and keep it in single digits."
Inflation in June was running at an annual rate of 4.8 percent, below the government's target of up to 6.5 percent for the year.
Many economists expect the rate to be above target this year as a result of the peso's more than six percent fall.

Ramos added that speculative attacks on the peso had come from both inside and outside the country and reiterated that the defence of the currencies of the Philippines and its neighbours should be based on strong cooperative action.

On Friday, foreign ministers of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) called for stronger cooperation to guard against "well coordinated" efforts to destabilise currencies in the region.
